metadata.note: The Avon, Geneseo and Mount Morris Railroad (AG&MM) served the Genesee Valley south of Rochester, connecting the villages of Avon, Geneseo, and Mount Morris (later extended to Dansville). Chartered as the Genesee Valley Railroad in 1856, it reached Geneseo and Mount Morris in January 1859, was reorganized as the AG&MM in 1860 after a foreclosure, and was leased to the Erie Railway in 1872 -- eventually becoming the Erie Railroad's 'Mount Morris Branch,' operated in conjunction with the Rochester and Genesee Valley Railroad's line into Rochester. Notably, the Erie fully electrified this branch (Rochester to Mount Morris) in 1906-1907, running it as an hourly electric commuter service until de-electrification began in 1934; passenger service between Rochester and Avon ended September 30 1941, and the line was abandoned in 1940-1941. GEOMETRY NOTE: Rochester-Avon and Mount Morris-Dansville are real-traced from OpenStreetMap active/abandoned rail tagging. The Avon-Geneseo-Mount Morris core segment is a straight-line approximation instead -- the OSM-tagged track in that stretch resolved to a real, connected path, but one that both backtracked (dipping south past Geneseo's latitude before turning back) and totaled roughly 50% longer than the sourced historic '15 miles' Avon-Mount Morris figure, indicating it traces a different, non-historic modern alignment rather than the original 1859 AG&MM route -- flagged honestly rather than presented as accurate track.

The Avon-Geneseo-Mount Morris stretch was rejected in favor of a straight-line approximation after its traced path both backtracked and measured ~50% longer than the sourced historic mileage for that stretch.

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.trim_note: 2026-08-24: this feature previously ran Rochester – Dansville, drawing the Rochester–Avon leg (the Rochester and Genesee Valley Railroad's line, opened 1853) as part of the AG&MM and from 1859, which both attributed it to the wrong company and started it six years late. That leg now lives in data/erie_rochester_branch.geojson, split by operator per Rule 4; this feature was cut back to Avon (its own railroad's actual north end) and relabelled Avon – Dansville. 49 leading vertices removed and replaced with the shared Avon endpoint -77.74880, 42.91243 so the two layers meet.

segments.note: The Erie electrified the entire line from its Court Street terminus in Rochester to Mount Morris in late 1906-March 1907; regular electric passenger service began May 12 1907 (test runs from April 1907), running hourly 6am-11:30pm and covering Rochester-Mount Morris in about 1 hour 10 minutes. De-electrification began in 1934, with gas-electric motor cars replacing the electric equipment. Frequency from real 1907 timetable detail (hourly).
